items.statement: Take responsibility for the performance qualification (PQ) of the computerised system, in addition to user acceptance testing (OQ) against the functional specification, which may include factory acceptance testing at the supplier.
items.quote: Apart from user acceptance testing (OQ) versus the functional specification, which may include ‘Factory Acceptance Testing’ (FAT), for example, at the supplier, the regulated user also has responsibility for the (PQ) performance qualification of the system.

items.statement: Perform the PQ user acceptance test in the system's operating environment against a User Requirements Specification that includes performance and quality acceptance protocols and criteria for both the controlling system and the controlled pharmaceutical process.
items.quote: In this context the PQ user acceptance test of the system is in its operating environment^3, and will again be against a User Requirements Specification (URS) that will include protocols and criteria for the performance and quality acceptance, not only for the controlling system but also for the controlled (pharmaceutical related) process application.

items.statement: Be able to show, through validation evidence, high confidence in the integrity of the processes run within the controlling computer system and of the processes it controls in the prescribed operating environment.
items.quote: The regulated user should be able to demonstrate through the validation evidence that they have a high level of confidence in the integrity of both the processes executed within the controlling computer system and in those processes controlled by the computer system within the prescribed operating environment.

items.statement: Ensure documented validation evidence for the system is available for review by GxP inspectors; the regulated user holds ultimate responsibility for this.

items.statement: Check that the supplier's software engineering processes cover design, coding, verification testing, integration and change control across the development life cycle, including after-sales support.
items.quote: This should include design, coding, verification testing, integration, and change control features of the development life cycle, (including after sales support).

items.statement: Evaluate the supplier's quality methodology for the design, construction, supply and maintenance of the software.
items.quote: In order for customers to have confidence in the reliability of the products, they should evaluate the quality methodology of the supplier for the design, construction, supply and maintenance of the software^4.

items.statement: Consider a formal, extensive review of the supplier company's history and the software package where extra assurance of software reliability is needed.
items.quote: A formal, extensive review of the history of the Supply Company and the software package may be an option to consider where an additional degree of assurance of the reliability of the software is needed.

items.statement: Document such a formal supplier review in a Supplier Audit Report.
items.quote: This should be documented in a Supplier Audit Report^5.

items.statement: Before purchase, consider known limitations and problems of the specific software packages or versions and whether the supplier's corrective actions are adequate.
items.quote: Prospective purchasers should consider any known limitations and problems for particular software packages or versions and the adequacy of any corrective actions by the Supplier.

items.statement: Support the final choice of software package with appropriate, comprehensive, documented customer acceptance testing.
items.quote: Appropriate, comprehensive documented customer acceptance testing should support the final selection of the software package.

items.statement: For standard software packages and COTS, stay vigilant to keep the systems reliable.
items.quote: For so called ‘standard software packages’ and COTS (as referenced in the GAMP guide and commercial literature), it is important that purchasers are vigilant in maintaining reliable systems.

items.statement: Record the conclusions and recommendations from reviews of own experience, literature and user group contacts on software problems.
items.quote: Conclusions and recommendations from such activities should be recorded.

items.statement: Where complex software cannot be directly assessed or fully evaluated, make sure a good construction process was used and properly documented.
items.quote: Where the reliability and structural integrity of complex software products cannot be directly assessed, or completely evaluated, then it is even more important to assure that a good construction process has been used and has been properly documented.

items.statement: Market research and focused quality system and product-specific audits of suppliers, by the user or an accredited third-party auditor, may be used for complex proprietary software.
items.quote: Market research plus focused quality system and product specific audits of the suppliers by the regulated user (or by an accredited third party auditor) may be beneficial here.

items.statement: For complex systems, obtain a high level of assurance that software development delivered a quality product that is structurally sound, clearly defined and controlled.
items.quote: For complex systems there should also be a high level of assurance that the development of the software has ensured delivery and operation of a quality product that is structurally sound, clearly defined and controlled.

items.statement: Develop and formally document test scripts and use them to show the system is installed, operating and performing satisfactorily.
items.quote: Test scripts should be developed, formally documented and used to demonstrate that the system has been installed, and is operating and performing satisfactorily.

items.statement: Relate the test scripts to the system's User Requirements Specifications and Functional Specifications.
items.quote: These test scripts should be related to the User Requirements Specifications and the Functional specifications for the system.

items.statement: Aim the testing schedule specifically at demonstrating validation of the system.
items.quote: This schedule of testing should be specifically aimed at demonstrating the validation of the system^22.

items.statement: Use satisfactory test results to confirm design validation.
items.quote: In software engineering terms satisfactory results obtained from the testing should confirm design validation.

items.statement: Apply additional IQ, OQ and PQ testing to processing equipment and activities related to or controlled by the computer system.
items.quote: Any processing equipment and activities related to or controlled by the computer system would require additional IQ, OQ and PQ testing regimes.

items.statement: If test phases and scopes are combined for a group of equipment or activities, define this in a test plan or strategy.
items.quote: It may be appropriate to combine test phases and test scopes for a group of equipment or activities, and this should be defined in a test plan or strategy.

items.statement: Be able to show formal acceptance of systems after testing and a controlled transfer into the live operational environment.
items.quote: Regulated Users should be able to demonstrate formal acceptance of systems after testing and controlled transfer into the live operational environment.

items.statement: Be able to provide evidence showing the range, complexity, functionality, control and validation status of the site's computerised systems.
items.quote: Regulated users need to be able to provide evidence for their computerised systems to demonstrate their range, complexity, functionality, control and validation status.

items.statement: Have a system that ensures formal assessment and reporting of quality and performance measures across all life-cycle stages: development, implementation, qualification and acceptance, operation, modification, re-qualification, maintenance and retirement.
items.quote: For the validation of computerised systems there should be a system in place that assures the formal assessment and reporting of quality and performance measures for all the life-cycle stages of software and system development, its implementation, qualification and acceptance, operation, modification, re-qualification, maintenance and retirement^23.

items.statement: Supplier or developer test scripts should be drafted under the project quality plan to verify performance against the functional specifications.

items.quote: The test scripts related to the user requirements specification are the responsibility of the regulated users.
